text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members frequently merge their code changes into a shared central repository. To manage this process, teams rely on CI pipelines, which are automated sequences of steps. Each time new code is pushed, the pipeline automatically triggers a build, compiling the project to check for technical errors. Following the build, a series of tests run automatically, from simple unit checks to more complex integration scenarios. If any step fails, developers are notified immediately. This approach allows teams to catch issues early in the development cycle, before they grow into major problems, keeping the software stable and release-ready.
